summary: The project consists of a smart, wearable electronic patch—a "Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring Patch"—designed to be attached to an astronaut's arm. It monitors vital signs and physiological changes while the astronaut is working both inside and outside the spacecraft, transmits this data to the International Space Station (ISS), and triggers an audible alarm whenever an abnormal reading is detected.
details:
on for the Astro Pulse (AstroPatch) Project

An Intelligent Nanotech Patch Powered by Edge AI and a Healing-Frequency Engine for Space Survival

Prepared by: Astro Pulse Team | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1) project Introduction and the Problem It Addresses (Introduction)

During long-duration space missions and extravehicular activities (EVA), astronauts face serious health, psychological, and environmental challenges. These risks include Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), resulting from increased intracranial pressure due to microgravity; acute cardiovascular stress; psychological stress and elevated cortisol levels; as well as the potentially fatal risk of accidental detachment from the International Space Station (EVA Tether Detachment).

The Astro Pulse project addresses this gap by developing an intelligent, wearable nanotech patch (AstroPatch) powered by a local artificial intelligence model (Edge AI). It monitors vital and environmental indicators in real time and provides immediate autonomous emergency intervention without relying on Earth-based communications, which are affected by latency.

2) project Objectives (Project Objectives

- Real-Time Biometric and Environmental Monitoring: Track 12 biological and environmental indicators inside the spacesuit with high accuracy and continuously for up to 14 days (336 hours).

- Early Detection Using Edge AI: Analyze data locally to detect SANS by monitoring optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) and assessing psychological and neurological status.

- Autonomous First Aid: Emit therapeutic sound frequencies (Solfeggio Frequencies) adapted to the type of risk in order to calm the nervous system and stabilize the pulse.

- Immediate Mechanical Rescue: Automatically activate safe nitrogen jets (SAFER) to stabilize the astronaut and return them in the event of detachment from the station

3)System Overview (System Overview)

The Astro Pulse system consists of a flexible medical nanotech patch (AstroPatch) attached directly to the astronaut's skin beneath the Extravehicular Mobility Unit (EMU) spacesuit. The patch integrates a multimodal sensing system with an ultra-low-power microcontroller (STM32U5) that runs medical analysis algorithms based on NASA's Human Research Program (NASA HRP).

When any deviation from the astronaut's personal baseline is detected, the system makes an independent decision within fractions of a second: either generating therapeutic sound waves through the Web Audio API engine, issuing local haptic and audible alerts, or activating mechanical protection systems and sending emergency data packets to the International Space Station (ISS).

4) Electronic Components (Hardware Components)

The system's physical architecture consists of 19 main and supporting components divided into three functional groups:

[First: Biometric and Environmental Sensor System — 12 Sensors]

* Item 01: Heart Rate Sensor | Scientific Name: ECG / PPG Sensor | Function: Measure heart rate and monitor changes in real time.

* Item 02: Blood Pressure Sensor | Scientific Name: Blood Pressure Monitoring System | Function: Measure systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

* Item 03: Body Temperature Sensor | Scientific Name: Digital Body Temperature Sensor | Function: Monitor the astronaut's core body temperature.

* Item 04: Blood Oxygen Saturation Sensor | Scientific Name: Pulse Oximeter (SpO2) | Function: Estimate the percentage of oxygen saturation in the blood.

* Item 05: Spacesuit Oxygen Sensor | Scientific Name: Oxygen Gas Sensor (O2) | Function: Measure oxygen concentration in the breathing air.

* Item 06: Spacesuit Pressure Sensor | Scientific Name: Absolute / Differential Pressure Sensor | Function: Monitor the internal pressure of the spacesuit.

* Item 07: Motion and Gravity Sensor | Scientific Name: Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) | Function: Measure acceleration and rotation and detect detachment.

* Item 08: Cortisol Sensor | Scientific Name: Electrochemical Cortisol Biosensor | Function: Analyze the level of the stress hormone cortisol.

* Item 09: Sweat Sensor | Scientific Name: Sweat Rate Sensor | Function: Monitor sweat rate and fluid loss.

* Item 10: Skin Response Sensor | Scientific Name: GSR / EDA Sensor | Function: Measure the skin's electrical conductance and assess psychological state.

* Item 11: Carbon Dioxide Sensor | Scientific Name: NDIR CO2 Sensor | Function: Measure carbon dioxide concentration inside the spacesuit.

* Item 12: Space Radiation Sensor | Scientific Name: Personal Radiation Dosimeter | Function: Record radiation dose and exposure rate.

[Second: Processing, Communication, and Power Units]

* Item 13: Main Controller | Scientific Name: STM32U5 Microcontroller (MCU) | Function: Collect data and run Edge AI models locally.

* Item 14: Space Communication Unit | Scientific Name: Space-to-Space EMU Radio (SSER) | Function: Transmit data and alerts to the ISS.

* Item 15: Audible Alert Unit | Scientific Name: Buzzer / Audible Alarm | Function: Issue an immediate audible alert when a fault is detected.

* Item 16: Vibration Alert Unit | Scientific Name: Vibration Motor | Function: Provide the astronaut with a tactile alert inside the spacesuit.

* Item 17: Space-Grade Battery | Scientific Name: Space-Qualified Battery | Function: Power the system for a target duration of 14 days (336 hours).

* Item 18: Battery Monitoring Unit | Scientific Name: Battery Monitoring System (BMS) | Function: Monitor voltage, current, state of charge, and temperature.

* Item 19: Power Regulation Unit | Scientific Name: Power Management Unit (PMU) | Function: Regulate voltages and distribute power with high efficiency.

[Third: Supporting and Structural Components]

* Component: Electronic Circuit Board | Scientific Name: Printed Circuit Board (PCB) | Function: Provide flexible electronic interconnections between components.

* Component: Sensor Reading Interfaces | Scientific Name: Sensor Interface Circuits | Function: Condition and filter analog signals before processing.

* Component: Data Logging Memory | Scientific Name: Non-Volatile Flash Memory | Function: Store readings locally when communication is lost.

* Component: Precision Timing Unit | Scientific Name: Real-Time Clock (RTC) | Function: Record an accurate timestamp for every reading.

* Component: Nanotech Patch Enclosure | Scientific Name: Wearable Patch Enclosure | Function: Protect the electronics and secure the patch safely to the skin.

* Component: Biometric Measurement Electrodes | Scientific Name: Biomedical Electrodes | Function: Capture cardiac and skin electrical signals

5) Software and Libraries Used (Software and Libraries)

- Primary Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES6+) for building the simulation model and telemetry application, and C/C++ for actual implementation on STM32U5 microcontrollers.

- Audio Generation Engine (Web Audio API): Use the AudioContext, OscillatorNode, and GainNode interfaces to generate precise-frequency therapeutic sound waves.

- Medical Analysis Algorithms: Analytical logic based on the standards of NASA's Human Research Program (NASA Human Research Program - HRP).

- Edge AI Architecture: Lightweight inference models to classify psychological and cardiac stress states locally without requiring a cloud connection

6) System Architecture and Data Flow Diagram (System Architecture)

Stage 1: The biometric and environmental sensors (12 Sensor Array) capture raw signals (ECG, BP, ONSD, Cortisol, GSR, IMU, Gases).

|--> Data moves to Stage 2: Signal-conditioning interfaces (Sensor Interface Circuits & ADC).

|--> Data moves to Stage 3: Main controller STM32U5 + Edge AI engine for decision-making:

- Normal-state path (OPTIMAL): Emit the balancing frequency 432Hz + periodic data logging.

- Early-warning path (WARNING): Emit frequency 528Hz/639Hz + adjust ambient lighting.

- Critical-state path (CRITICAL): Multi-path emergency response including:

1) Audio: Emergency frequency 174Hz (triangle wave).

2) Local: Vibration + audible Buzzer alarm.

3) Mechanical: Activate SAFER nitrogen jets.

4) Space communication: Send an emergency transmission via SSER Radio to the ISS.

7) code Explanation and the Function of Each Part (Code Explanation)

The system's core software has been built within the AstroPatchSensor software class, which manages the data lifecycle from the moment of acquisition through therapeutic intervention:

- Constructor: Initializes the astronaut's identity, battery level (96%), network status (5G Mesh), and stores the astronaut's personal baseline for vital values (Baseline: heart rate 65 bpm, blood pressure 118 mmHg, glucose 92 mg/dL, optic nerve sheath diameter ONSD 4.6 mm, and cortisol 12 µg/dL). It also defines a dictionary of therapeutic Solfeggio frequencies (432, 528, 639, 285, and 174 Hz).

- Telemetry reading and analysis function readTelemetry(currentVitals): Receives real-time readings and creates an immediate report containing the timestamp, status, warnings, recommended frequency, and required action. The function checks two critical pathways: first, the ONSD indicator for detecting SANS (warning at >= 5.1 mm, and critical risk at >= 5.8 mm, with a recommendation to activate the LBNP negative-pressure suit); second, cardiac stress screening (heart rate > 115) or detachment from the station (isDetached), to activate the SAFER nitrogen jets.

- Therapeutic frequency emission function emitHealingFrequency(frequencyHz): Creates an audio context through the Web Audio API and generates a sound wave through OscillatorNode. The function selects a triangle wave in emergencies (174 Hz) to increase neurological alerting, and a calm sine wave for other conditions, applying a smooth audio ramp (linearRampToValueAtTime) over 0.15 seconds to protect the astronaut's ears from sudden sound changes.

- Frequency stop function stopFrequency(): Gradually reduces the sound level to zero over 0.1 seconds, then stops the oscillator and safely disconnects it from memory to prevent any clicking noise (Audio Clicks).

[Approved System Source Code — AstroPatch Telemetry & Audio Engine]

class AstroPatchSensor {

constructor(astronautName) {

this.astronautName = astronautName;

this.batteryLevel = 96;

this.signalStrength = "Optimal (5G Mesh)";

this.isMonitoring = true;

this.baseline = { heartRate: 65, systolicBP: 118, glucose: 92, onsd: 4.6, cortisol: 12 };

this.healingFrequencies = { optimal: 432, cardio: 528, immune: 639, bones: 285, emergency: 174 };

this.audioCtx = null; this.oscillator = null; this.gainNode = null;

}

readTelemetry(currentVitals) {

const report = {

timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), status: "OPTIMAL",

warnings: [], recommendedFrequency: this.healingFrequencies.optimal, actionRequired: "None"

};

if (currentVitals.onsd >= 5.8) {

report.status = "CRITICAL";

report.warnings.push("Acute Intracranial Pressure / SANS Risk detected.");

report.recommendedFrequency = this.healingFrequencies.emergency;

report.actionRequired = "Engage LBNP negative pressure suit & transmit ultrasound to Houston.";

} else if (currentVitals.onsd >= 5.1) {

report.status = "WARNING";

report.warnings.push("Early ONSD expansion above 5.0mm threshold.");

report.actionRequired = "Perform warm circadian lighting adjustment.";

}

if (currentVitals.heartRate > 115 || currentVitals.isDetached) {

report.status = "CRITICAL";

report.warnings.push("High cardiovascular stress or EVA Tether Detachment!");

report.recommendedFrequency = this.healingFrequencies.emergency;

report.actionRequired = "Activate SAFER nitrogen thrusters and engage diaphragmatic breathing.";

}

return report;

}

emitHealingFrequency(frequencyHz) {

const AudioContext = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext;

if (!this.audioCtx) this.audioCtx = new AudioContext();

if (this.audioCtx.state === 'suspended') this.audioCtx.resume();

if (this.oscillator) { try { this.oscillator.stop(); } catch (e) {} }

this.oscillator = this.audioCtx.createOscillator();

this.gainNode = this.audioCtx.createGain();

this.oscillator.type = frequencyHz === 174 ? 'triangle' : 'sine';

this.oscillator.frequency.setValueAtTime(frequencyHz, this.audioCtx.currentTime);

this.gainNode.gain.setValueAtTime(0, this.audioCtx.currentTime);

this.gainNode.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.2, this.audioCtx.currentTime + 0.15);

this.oscillator.connect(this.gainNode);

this.gainNode.connect(this.audioCtx.destination);

this.oscillator.start();

return true;

}

}

8) How Readings Are Processed and Analyzed (Data Processing)

Astro Pulse's data-processing methodology relies on edge computing to avoid any response delay:

- Personal Baseline Calibration: Instead of relying on general averages, real-time readings are compared with the individual astronaut's biometric profile recorded before the mission.

- Multi-Tier Thresholding: Automatically classify the condition into three levels: normal (OPTIMAL), early warning (WARNING), and critical (CRITICAL), based on embedded logical rules.

- Biometric and Environmental Sensor Fusion: Correlate motion acceleration (IMU) with heart rate to distinguish normal physical exertion from panic or space detachment events

9. Health and Environmental Indicators Monitored by the System (Health Indicators)

* Category 1: Cardiac and Blood Indicators

- Measured indicators: Heart rate (HR), blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO2).

- Reference thresholds: Baseline heart rate 65 bpm (critical warning at > 115 bpm).

* Category 2: Neurological and Visual Indicators

- Measured indicators: Optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD).

- Reference thresholds: Normal 4.6 mm | Warning >= 5.1 mm | SANS risk >= 5.8 mm.

* Category 3: Psychological and Hormonal Indicators

- Measured indicators: Cortisol level, skin response (GSR), sweating.

- Reference thresholds: Baseline cortisol 12 µg/dL for detecting acute stress.

* Category 4: Spacesuit Environmental Indicators

- Measured indicators: O2 and CO2 concentrations, spacesuit pressure, radiation dose.

- Reference thresholds: Ensure breathing-environment safety and protection from cosmic radiation.

10. Actual Testing and Results (Testing and Results)

The project is currently in the preliminary modeling and software simulation stage (Simulation & Prototype Validation), and software tests have produced the following results:

- SANS Scenario Test: When the ONSD indicator was simulated at 5.2 mm, the system immediately transitioned to WARNING and recommended adjusting the lighting. When it was increased to 5.9 mm, the system changed to CRITICAL and emitted a 174 Hz frequency.

- Space Detachment Scenario Test (EVA Detachment): When the variable (isDetached = true) was activated or the heart rate exceeded 115 beats per minute, the system responded within fractions of a second by issuing a command to activate the SAFER nitrogen jets and play the emergency frequency.

- Audio Engine Stability: Gain Ramping successfully prevented any distortion or sudden buzzing when switching between different therapeutic frequencies.

11. System Limitations and Safety Precautions (Limitations and Safety)

- Preliminary Design Stage: The current component list represents an initial engineering design; the prototype is not suitable for actual space use until it has passed thermal-vacuum, vibration, and space-medical qualification tests.

- Power Budget: Operating 12 sensors for 336 hours (14 days) requires strict power-consumption management through the STM32U5 microcontroller's deep-sleep mode (STM32U5 Low-Power Modes) and actual battery-discharge testing.

- Compatibility with the SSER Radio: The communication protocols and connection interfaces of the Space-to-Space EMU Radio unit must be carefully verified before final integration.

- Audio Software Limitations: The Web Audio API engine requires an initial interaction to activate the audio context in browser environments. Therapeutic frequencies are also a supplementary support measure and do not replace direct medical intervention by the station crew

12. Conclusion and References (Conclusion and References)

The Astro Pulse project presents an integrated vision for the future of autonomous healthcare in space. By combining precise nanotech sensing, edge artificial intelligence, and immediate audio and mechanical intervention, the AstroPatch patch provides an intelligent protective shield that enhances astronaut survival and safety in the harshest cosmic environments.

Scientific References and Applicable Standards:

- NASA Human Research Program (HRP): Standards for monitoring SANS and astronauts' vital indicators.

- NASA-STD-3001: Standards for human-space-system integration and the safety of extravehicular mobility units (EMU / SAFER).

- W3C Web Audio API Specification: Standards for digital audio-frequency processing and generation.

- STMicroelectronics STM32U5 Datasheet: Technical characteristics of low-power microcontrollers designed for medical and space applications.Comprehensive Engineering Documentati
